newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler profit, sales to climb through 1999 - report.
newsitem.headline: Daimler profit, sales to climb through 1999 - report.

text.p: The German magazine "Capital" said on Wednesday that Daimler-Benz AG expects 1997 operating profit to climb 400 million marks ($234.6 million) to 3.675 billion marks and that sales will climb to 111 billion marks from 103 billion marks.
A Daimler-Benz spokesman said the expected results figures had already been released more than a year ago as part of its planning for the wind-down of its AEG AG unit.

The magazine said in a summary of an article to appear in its next edition that according to internal Daimler plans, sales at Daimler's main units Mercedes-Benz, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG and Debis AG will climb to 130 billion marks by 1999.
Operating profit at those units, meanwhile, was expected to climb to 6.3 billion marks by 1999, the article added.
The magazine said the figures were adjusted to reflect accounting changes at Daimler.
Capital also said that Daimler plans to cut 9,000 jobs through the 1999 as part of ongoing efforts to trim costs and lead to higher profits at all it operating units.

Schrempp, the magazine said, especially hopes to boost results at Mercedes-Benz. Sales at the car and truck maker were seen increasing to more than 100 billion marks by 1999 and profits to five billion marks.
A Daimler spokesman said the figures were "nothing new" and were part of an internal report first made public more than a year ago.
